script: Spread and total were not saved for SF at SEA, so the SF-SEA script is form only: SEA is Emanuel Wilson on the ground (51 carries, 187 yards in weeks 2-4) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba through the air (31 targets, 359 yards), while SF is Christian McCaffrey as the carry engine (40 carries, 150 yards) with George Kittle (17 targets, 232 yards) and Mike Evans (17 targets, 164 yards). SF defense allowed 6 passes of 20-plus on 150 throws and only 3 runs of 10-plus, and SEA defense allowed 5 passes of 20-plus on 135 throws, so SF at SEA reads as alpha volume rather than a track meet.
who_goes_off: SEA's Jaxon Smith-Njigba should go off at 119.7 receiving yards a game on 31 targets against an SF defense that allowed 6.38 YPA in the middle and 6.0 to the left, and SEA quarterback Sam Darnold's EPA stays 0.20 on 52 blitzed dropbacks versus 0.19 clean so SF's 31% blitz rate does not take him off his spot. SF's George Kittle is the other piece, 77.3 yards a game with 232 receiving yards on only 146 air yards, a YAC path that does not need the 20-plus throws SEA has allowed just 5 times.
weak_spot: SEA's pass defense is tight everywhere, but the left side is the relative hole at 5.9 YPA on 51 attempts versus 4.79 in the middle (19 attempts) and 4.69 right (54 attempts), and SEA also leaked 9 runs of 10-plus at 3.73 YPC. SF's soft spot is the middle at 6.38 YPA, with the left at 6.0 on 56 attempts the bigger sample, while SF run defense is not the leak at 3.76 YPC and only 3 runs of 10-plus.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for SF at SEA, so there is no injury fallout to price for either SF or SEA, and roles are read only off weeks 2-4 usage for SF's Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle and SEA's Emanuel Wilson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
qb_vs_blitz: SF quarterback Brock Purdy is a different passer against pressure, 1.08 EPA per dropback on 40 blitzed dropbacks versus 0.31 when the defense sits, and SEA blitzes only 21%, so Purdy is more likely to live in the worse split in this SF-SEA game. SEA quarterback Sam Darnold does not care in this sample, 0.20 EPA versus the blitz on 52 dropbacks and 0.19 without, so SF's 31% blitz rate does not downgrade SEA's Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

picks.why: SEA receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 359 yards on 31 targets over the last three games, 119.7 a game, against a 95.5 line, and SF has allowed 6.38 YPA in the middle plus 6.0 to the left while SEA's Sam Darnold stays at 0.20 EPA when SF blitzes at 31%. SF has allowed only 6 passes of 20-plus on 150 throws, but a 24-yard cushion over 95.5 still holds if that 10-plus target pace stays intact in SF at SEA.

SF tight end George Kittle has 232 yards on 17 targets, 77.3 a game, versus a 54.5 line, and 146 air yards means about 86 of those yards came after the catch so SEA allowing only 5 passes of 20-plus on 135 attempts does not close the path. SEA's middle is their best location at 4.79 YPA on 19 attempts, and that still leaves a 23-yard gap between Kittle's weeks 2-4 form and 54.5 in this SF-SEA game.
